23:["$","p",null,{"children":["The true posterior is trimodal: three peaks of equal mass, and a lot of nearly-zero corridor\nbetween them. Hand that posterior to a Gaussian filter and it must answer with a mean and a\ncovariance. Moment-match it honestly and the mean lands at the centroid of three separated\nhypotheses — a location the evidence never argued for, and one the robot is at most a third likely\nto be near — while the covariance inflates until it spans the corridor, reporting an uncertainty\nthat is technically correct and operationally useless. Let the filter track a single mode instead,\nas an EKF started near one door will, and it becomes ",["$","em",null,{"children":"confidently wrong"}]," two times out of three\nwith nothing in its state to record that a choice was ever made."]}]
24:["$","p",null,{"children":"This is not a tuning problem. A Gaussian has one mode; the posterior has three; the mismatch is\nstructural. So represent the belief with something that can hold three answers at once."}]

27:["$","p",null,{"children":[["$","strong",null,{"children":"The cloud is a distribution, not a list of guesses."}]," The dashed purple line is the weighted\nmean, and during the multimodal phase it wanders across the corridor tracking the ",["$","em",null,{"children":"centroid"}]," of the\nsurviving hypotheses rather than any one of them. That is not a bug in the readout — it is the\ncorrect expectation of a genuinely multimodal belief, and it is exactly the number a Gaussian\nfilter would have been forced to report. The particles are the answer; the mean is a lossy summary\nof them, and in this corridor it is the worst summary available."]}]
28:["$","p",null,{"children":[["$","strong",null,{"children":"Weighting and resampling are different operations, and only one of them destroys anything."}],"\nDuring the green phase nothing moves: the ticks change size because their weights changed. During\nthe purple phase nothing changes size: the ticks ",["$","em",null,{"children":"move"}],", because low-weight hypotheses were\ndeleted and high-weight ones were cloned. Weighting is reversible bookkeeping. Resampling is\nselection, and selection is irreversible."]}]
29:["$","p",null,{"children":[["$","strong",null,{"children":"Diversity is a finite resource."}]," Press ",["$","em",null,{"children":"Deprivation preset"}]," — 30 particles, a razor-sharp\nsensor — and re-roll the seed a few times. In a sizeable fraction of runs every particle near\nRusty dies in one unlucky weighting, and from then on the filter converges tightly and confidently\nonto the wrong door and never recovers. It cannot recover: resampling only ever redistributes\nhypotheses that already exist, and the motion noise is far too small to walk one back."]}]
